connection: Session 28 deliberately observed a faulted Task. Session 28B keeps production synchronous and uses ScratchPad to distinguish cooperative cancellation from unexpected failure.
objectives: Explain that cancellation is a request rather than forced termination.
Distinguish the CancellationTokenSource that owns a request from the CancellationToken that carries it.
Forward one token through an async helper to Task.Delay.
Await canceled work and deliberately handle OperationCanceledException.
Dispose the source and deliberately await every created Task.

visuals.title: Source owns; token carries
visuals.explanation: CancellationTokenSource owns the cancellation request. Its Token value carries that request to cooperating code but cannot issue the request itself.

visuals.title: Forward one request
visuals.explanation: RunAsync passes one token to ProcessReportAsync, which forwards that same token to Task.Delay. A parameter alone does nothing unless code observes or forwards it.

visuals.title: Observation has a timeline
visuals.explanation: Work starts, Cancel requests a stop, Task.Delay observes the token, and await surfaces OperationCanceledException to the deliberate caller.

visuals.title: Canceled is not faulted
visuals.explanation: This expected cooperative stop differs from Session 28's InvalidOperationException, which represented an unexpected operation failure.

preQuiz.explanation: The source owns and issues the request; the token carries it.

preQuiz.prompt: Does adding a CancellationToken parameter automatically stop work?
options: No; code must observe or forward it
preQuiz.explanation: Cancellation is cooperative, so participating code must use the token.

preQuiz.prompt: Does async automatically create another thread?
preQuiz.explanation: async and await describe asynchronous control flow, not a requirement for another thread.

concept.title: Cancellation is cooperative
paragraphs: Cancel requests that participating work stop. It does not forcibly terminate a method or thread.
CancellationTokenSource creates and controls the request. CancellationToken is the value passed through the call chain. The source is disposable and should be used in a using declaration.
concept.code:
using CancellationTokenSource cancellationSource = new();
CancellationToken cancellationToken = cancellationSource.Token;

concept.title: A token must reach an observer
paragraphs: A CancellationToken parameter has no effect by itself. RunAsync forwards one token to ProcessReportAsync, and the helper forwards it to Task.Delay.

Read Task Delay(int millisecondsDelay, CancellationToken cancellationToken) one parameter at a time: millisecondsDelay is the intended wait, while cancellationToken carries a request that Delay can observe. The same token is forwarded rather than replaced.

concept.title: Canceled work is observed through await
paragraphs: When Task.Delay observes the request, awaiting the canceled operation normally throws OperationCanceledException. This experiment catches it where RunAsync deliberately translates cancellation into learner-visible output.
This is expected control flow for the experiment, unlike Session 28's InvalidOperationException fault. Task.Delay only simulates waiting here; it is not production I/O.

concept.title: Task ownership still applies
paragraphs: Awaiting Task observes completion, cancellation, or failure but produces no assignable value. Awaiting Task<T> produces a T value.
Therefore await experiment.RunAsync(); observes the Task. It does not discard it. A bare unawaited call or _ = experiment.RunAsync(); gives up deliberate completion control.
concept.code: await experiment.RunAsync(); // observed; no result variable

lab.title: Request and Observe Cooperative Cancellation
lab.objective: Pass one cancellation request through a simulated report operation, observe it through await, and distinguish cancellation from failure.
lab.task: Build CooperativeCancellationExperiments in permanent Session28B ScratchPad code without changing production.
lab.startingCondition: Install .NET SDK 10.0.302, as required by global.json. The working branch has completed Session 28 and awaits AsyncFailureExperiments from ScratchPad Program.cs.

steps.text: In project src/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.ScratchPad, create folder Session28B and file src/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.ScratchPad/Session28B/CooperativeCancellationExperiments.cs.
In CooperativeCancellationExperiments.cs, declare public sealed class CooperativeCancellationExperiments. Keep it in the global namespace, matching the learner repository.

Inside CooperativeCancellationExperiments, add public Task RunAsync() with no parameters. Do not add async yet. Temporarily return Task.CompletedTask because a non-async Task method must explicitly return a Task object; void would give the caller no completion handle.
steps.purposeAfter: You now have a distinct experiment with a warning-free completion contract. Next you will create the operation that can receive a cancellation request.

steps.text: Inside the class but outside RunAsync, add private Task ProcessReportAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken). Do not add async yet. Temporarily return Task.CompletedTask. The token parameter carries a request but provides no behavior until code observes or forwards it.

In ProcessReportAsync, add async to the declaration and remove return Task.CompletedTask. Await Task.Delay with an intended 2000 millisecond wait and the existing cancellationToken parameter. This overload reads Task Delay(int millisecondsDelay, CancellationToken cancellationToken): the first argument sets the intended wait and the second lets Delay observe the forwarded request. Task.Delay simulates waiting, not production I/O.

Still in ProcessReportAsync, print that report processing started immediately before the delay, and print that report processing completed after the await. Do not create a replacement token. async and await do not automatically create another thread.
steps.purposeAfter: The helper now cooperates by forwarding its token to an observing API. If cancellation arrives during the delay, its completion message will not run and await will expose cancellation to the caller.

steps.text: In RunAsync, add async to the declaration and remove return Task.CompletedTask. Create a CancellationTokenSource in a using declaration named cancellationSource so it is disposed when RunAsync ends. Store cancellationSource.Token in a CancellationToken variable named cancellationToken.

In RunAsync, call ProcessReportAsync with cancellationToken and store the returned Task in processingTask. Parentheses invoke ProcessReportAsync and return its Task; processingTask is that stored Task object and will later be awaited without parentheses.
After creating processingTask, print Cancellation requested. Then call Cancel on cancellationSource. Cancel requests cooperation; it does not forcibly terminate code or cancel a thread.
steps.purposeAfter: RunAsync now owns a source, starts one operation with its token, and requests cancellation. The remaining work deliberately awaits the stored Task so the request cannot become unobserved background work.

steps.text: In RunAsync, add try and catch for OperationCanceledException. Inside try, await processingTask without parentheses. Awaiting Task observes completion or cancellation but produces no assignable result; Task<T> would produce a T value.

Inside the OperationCanceledException catch, print Cancellation observed and handled. Catch here because RunAsync deliberately translates this expected request into experiment output; do not confuse it with Session 28's InvalidOperationException fault.

In src/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.ScratchPad/Program.cs, immediately after the Session 28 call, print a Session 28B heading, create CooperativeCancellationExperiments, and await RunAsync. Do not assign the awaited expression to var. Awaiting the Task observes it; a bare call or assigning the Task to _ would discard deliberate completion control.
steps.purposeAfter: The experiment now has an awaited top-level caller, so ScratchPad owns its completion and cancellation handling. Next you will run it to verify the request travels through the whole chain.

steps.text: From the csharp-practice-working solution folder, run ScratchPad in Release. Verify output shows processing started, cancellation requested, and cancellation observed and handled; the processing-completed message should not appear.
steps.purposeAfter: The focused run checks the observable cancellation timeline. The final validation checks that adding this permanent experiment did not damage the cumulative solution.

steps.text: Build PinkMachine19.TimeClock.sln in Release, then run the complete tests without rebuilding. Open Solution Reveal only after both pass.
steps.code:
dotnet build PinkMachine19.TimeClock.sln --configuration Release
dotnet test PinkMachine19.TimeClock.sln --configuration Release --no-build

reveals.title: Solution
reveals.text: One source owns the request, one token is forwarded, and every Task is awaited.

lab.expectedBehavior:
Report processing started.
Cancellation requested.
Cancellation observed and handled.
lab.validation: dotnet run --project src/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.ScratchPad/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.ScratchPad.csproj --configuration Release && dotnet build PinkMachine19.TimeClock.sln --configuration Release && dotnet test PinkMachine19.TimeClock.sln --configuration Release --no-build

expectedFiles.why: Keep the lesson synchronized with the cumulative build step.

review: CancellationTokenSource is disposed and owns the request.
One CancellationToken is forwarded to ProcessReportAsync and Task.Delay.
Every created Task is deliberately awaited.
Cancellation is reported separately from an unexpected fault.

postQuiz.prompt: Why did ProcessReportAsync stop during Task.Delay?
options: Delay observed the forwarded token after Cancel requested cancellation
postQuiz.explanation: The source requested cancellation and the token carried it to an observing API.

postQuiz.prompt: Why is await processingTask written without parentheses?
options: processingTask is already a Task object
The Task has a string result
postQuiz.explanation: Parentheses were used when calling the helper; the stored Task is awaited directly.

postQuiz.prompt: What value can be assigned from awaiting RunAsync?
postQuiz.explanation: Task represents completion but has no result value; Task<T> supplies T.

reflections: Where would cancellation be lost if the helper ignored its parameter?
Why does the source belong to the code deciding when to cancel?
Why is OperationCanceledException expected here but InvalidOperationException was a fault in Session 28?
whatBreaks: Removing the token from Task.Delay makes the helper ignore the request. Removing await processingTask gives up deliberate observation. Removing the using declaration leaves the source undisposed. Catching InvalidOperationException would not translate the expected cancellation.
summary: Cooperative cancellation travels from a CancellationTokenSource through one CancellationToken to observing code. Cancel requests a stop; Task.Delay observes it; await surfaces OperationCanceledException; and the deliberate caller handles that outcome without treating it as an unexpected fault.
